items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: It's like Tommy Dorsey playing -- everyone wants to play it exactly like they play it.

ctx.x: Would there be much of what you might call improvised solo playing in those days -- I imagine it would be mostly a matter of taking a break or a few bars or something.

Yes. There was much improvising. And a lot of times -- you know -- guys would take something somebody else had played they'd heard played -- you know -- put it in there. It's like they used to play a regular trombone solo on -- they thought it was a really great thing to do you know. Play it -- sing on the road.

And if it was a masterpiece thing -- everyone wants to play it today -- they try to play (singing) -- but you know invariably they'd want to play his solo. Everybody -- you know -- but it's (inaudible) they're playing really. It's a nostalgic theme and it's -- and it's like Tommy Dorsey playing -- everyone wants to play it exactly like they play it.
